peer_results.rationale: Candidate amd_2024_7_D050 focuses narrowly on the components of working capital cash flows (collections, inventory, employee expenses) without addressing the broader liquidity requirements, debt service, or capital expenditure drivers that characterize AVGO's Item 7 disclosure. Candidate amd_2024_7_D049 discusses liquidity sufficiency and capital market access rather than the specific drivers of liquidity needs (such as debt, capex, or working capital volumes) detailed by AVGO.

comparisons.peer_summary: Short-term funding covers capital expenditures, working capital, restructuring costs, partner distributions, and strategic investments, while long-term requirements incrementally contemplate significant manufacturing expansion and process technology investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC identify capital expenditures, working capital, and strategic investments/acquisitions as primary drivers of liquidity requirements. AVGO explicitly lists '$69,847 million of outstanding indebtedness' as a key liquidity driver (P063_S001), whereas INTC's disclosure for item 7 focuses on funding structures including 'short-term funding requirements include capital expenditures... working capital requirements' and 'long-term funding requirements incrementally contemplate investments in significant manufacturing expansion' (P092_S004, P092_S006). While AVGO quantifies its debt load as a specific liquidity drain, INTC details its capital spending roadmap and restructuring costs as the composition of its funding needs.

sentences.text: Our short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from: (i) business acquisitions and investments we may make from time to time, (ii) working capital requirements, (iii) research and development and capital expenditure needs, (iv) cash dividend payments (if and when declared by our Board of Directors), (v) interest and principal payments related to our $69,847 million of outstanding indebtedness, and (vi) payment of income taxes.

Our short-term funding requirements include capital expenditures for worldwide manufacturing and assembly and test, including investments in our process technology roadmap; investments in our product roadmap; working capital requirements, including cash outlays associated with the 2024 Restructuring Plan; partner distributions to our non-controlling interest holders; and strategic investments.
Our long-term funding requirements incrementally contemplate investments in significant manufacturing expansion plans and investments to accelerate our process technology.

comparisons.peer_summary: For 2024, net cash used for investing activities consisted primarily of $8.39 billion in expenditures for property, plant, and equipment and $205 million in net outflows from available-for-sale securities, partially offset by $315 million in government incentives for capital expenditures.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose significant capital expenditure requirements as a major component of their liquidity needs. AVGO states it 'expect[s] capital expenditures to be higher in the fiscal year ending November 2, 2025' (P063_S003) as part of its liquidity drivers. MU provides specific 2024 capital expenditure figures, noting '$8.39 billion of expenditures for property, plant, and equipment' and that it received '$315 million received from government incentives to offset capital expenditures' (P040_S001). Both disclosures highlight capex as a critical use of cash that drives liquidity requirements.

AVGO lists 'working capital requirements' and 'research and development and capital expenditure needs' as primary sources of liquidity requirements (P063_S001). QCOM similarly details 'Recent and expected working and other capital requirements' including '$12.8 billion' in purchase obligations and '$1.0 billion' in capital expenditures for fiscal 2024 (P044_S003, P044_S005). sentences.text: Our short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from: (i) business acquisitions and investments we may make from time to time, (ii) working capital requirements, (iii) research and development and capital expenditure needs, (iv) cash dividend payments (if and when declared by our Board of Directors), (v) interest and principal payments related to our $69,847 million of outstanding indebtedness, and (vi) payment of income taxes.

• Cash outflows for capital expenditures were $1.0 billion in fiscal 2024 and $1.5 billion in fiscal 2023. We expect capital expenditures to increase from fiscal 2024 in the near term to support our production and testing needs related to our growth and diversification initiatives.

• Our purchase obligations at September 29, 2024, which primarily relate to purchase commitments with certain suppliers of our integrated circuit products, including those under multi-year capacity commitments, totaled $12.8 billion, of which, $9.6 billion is expected to be paid in the next 12 months.
